sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 26.03.2022 at about 9.45 a.m, the petitioner was riding the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-V-9299 from Kannamangala towards Bengaluru,
slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Devanahalli Toll, B.B.Road, Devanahalli, Benglauru City, at that time the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-40-N-1854 driven the same from Devanahalli towards Bengaluru, drove the same from right side to left side of the bike in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed to the left side of the petitioner's motorcycle and touched the left side of the bike handle, due to the said impact the petitioner unable to control his motorcycle.
As a result of which he fell down from his motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediatly after the accident he was shifted to Manasa Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of car.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. After service of notice, respondent No.1 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-40-N-1854.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle /
petitioner who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid &
effective DL and further the said insured vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 appeared through her counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent has denied that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
The respondent No.2 admitted that she is the RC owner of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-40-N-1854 and was duly insured with the 1st respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.

It is further urged that in case if court comes to conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for any compensation same is to be fastened on the Suhas.R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39698896/

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 26.03.2022 at about 9.45 a.m., near Devanahalli Toll, B.B.Road,
Devanahalli, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-40-N-1854 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 24 were marked on his behalf.

Dr.S.A.
Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW.2.
Ex.P.21 & 22 were marked through him.
The respondent No.1 did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondents counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of car for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
10. Further the IO has issued notice u/s 133 of MV Act as per Ex.P.7, the owner of the offending vehicle has replied to the notice u/s 133 of IMV Act as per Ex.P.8.
The owner of the offending vehicle has admitted the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Therefore it is crystal clear that the offending vehicle is caused accident and in the accident the petitioner sustained injury.
Therefore the respondents have not placed any material to show there is a negligence on the part of the petitioner in the accident.
Further The police documents spells out there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car.

Further the police records and oral and documentary evidence of the petitioner are proved that the accident was occurred on the sole negligence of driver of offending Suhas.R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39698896/
3 car bearing Reg.No.KA-40-N-1854.

sentences.text: Though PW.1 was cross-examined at length by respondent No.1 counsel but nothing fatal was elicited so as to distrust the petitioner's version in his chief-examination.
The petitioner has satisfactorily proved that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-40-N-1854 in the accident.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the car.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
12. As per the medical records petitioner has sustained the following injury : (i) Communited fracture of right TIBIAL condyle.
It is needless to say that the said injury is grievous in nature.

13. The 2-Discharge summaries issued by Manasa hospital, Bengaluru which is marked at Ex.P.19 indicate that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 26.03.2022 to 30.03.2022 (5 days) and from 20.07.2023 to 24.07.2023 (5 days).
In total he took treatment for a period of 10 days.

During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : 1) ORIF with LCP for tibial condyle (2) Bone grafting under SA on 27.03.2022 and Implant removal under SA on 21.07.2023.
14. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY :
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he examined an Orthopedic Surgeon by name Dr. S.A. Somashekar as PW.2 who deposed that on clinical examination, he found that the petitioner has 36% disability to the right lower limb and 18% whole body physical disability.

It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.2 that he has not treated the petitioner and at the time of discharge,
the condition of petitioner is stable.
He further admitted that fractures is malunited.
He admitted that though petitioner has no injury in hip, he has assessed the disability in respect of hip.
Witness volunteer there is stiffness at hip.
He further admitted that there is no shortening and nerve damage.
He categorically admitted that the petitioner can do his day-to- day work with some difficulty.
15. Further it is to be seen whether the aforesaid disability impairs the avocation of the petitioner.
As per the averments made in his evidence affidavit, at the time of accident the petitioner was working as System Engineer in Infosys Company and earning Rs.67,000/- p.m.
In order to substantiate the above said fact petitioner has produced Job ID card and 4- Salary slips from February-2022 to May-2022 at Ex.P.12 and 14.
PW.1 stated that after the accident he could not do any work for undergoing treatment from the date of accident till today, thereby he lost his earnings and future earnings from the date of accident.

During the course of cross examination by learned counsel for respondent No.1 the PW.1 admitted that at the time of accident he was getting salary for a sum of Rs.25,000/- and now he was getting salary of Rs.31,000/-.
Further he admitted that now also he was working in the same company.

sentences.text: This Court also does not loose sight on the fact that even PW.1 himself had categorically admitted with regard to his future income as here under : "at the time of accident he was getting salary for a sum of Rs.25,000/- and now he was getting salary of Rs.31,000/- and now also he was working in the same company.
It could be ascertained from the materials placed on record and the admission of PW.l himself that now he was working in same Company and getting salary.

17. In view of the decision reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 in the case of Subhash V/s New India Assurance Co.Ltd., 'If the claimant has continued in service, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.'

entities.text: Subhash V/s New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That is to say as the actual financial loss arising out of physical disability is not made out by the claimant, he is not entitled for compensation towards 'loss of future income'.
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
As referred above, considering the nature of injuries, treatment given, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for some days.
Further petitioner stated that due to the accidental injuries he was unable to attend his duties and thereby he lost his earnings.
In his cross examination PW.1 stated that he was on leave for 1 month after the accident, of which approximately 12 days of salary were paid, the remaining days were not paid.
Further he admitted that he has not produced the attendance register.
He stated that he has produced documents to show that he was not paid on the holiday.
The salary certificate says LOP of 4 days.
It means payment not paid for when he was absent due to accident.
He further admitted that his company has not issued leave certificate, therefore he unable to produce the same.

Further on perusal of salary slip for the month of April-2022, wherein it is clearly depicts that there is mentioned 4 days of LOP and in the deductions / particulars column it is mentioned salary recovery of Rs.7,090/-.

Thus by taking into account the income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.7,090/- which is rounded off to Rs.7,100/- under this head.
19. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
Petitioner has suffered multiple fracture injuries.
As such, necessarily he had undergone pain and mental agony.

Thus, this tribunal awards a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
20. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 10 days is proved with the help of Discharge summary.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care by leaving their duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day and a sum of Rs.15,000/- (1,500 X 10) is awarded under this head.
21. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
9-Medical bills produced by PW.1 is marked at Ex.P15.
As per that, the claimant has spent Rs.8,618/- towards medical expenses.
And further 39-Medical bills produced for a sum of Rs.33,425/-.
During the course of his cross examination he categorically admitted that he has taken out Rs.1,56,000/- from health insurance, i.e. Mediclaim, and he has paid the remaining amount.
Further he admitted that the inpatient bill has been reimbursed from his department but Suhas.

On perusal of Ex.P.15 are the medical bills.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.23 bills the Sl.No.1 and 2 are the ambulance bills.
The Sl.No.5 and 8 are the advance bills, they are not considered.
In the calculation memo the petitioner has deducted the amount of Rs.5,000/- and Rs.5,903/-= Rs.10,903/- as the same is advance bills.
Further rest of the bills shows that the petitioner has purchased medicines.

Hence the petitioner is entitled a sum of Rs.8,618/-
under the Ex.P.15 and a sum of Rs.33,425/- under the Ex.P.23.

Hence in total a sum of Rs.42,043/-,
which is rounded off to Rs.42,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The age of the petitioner was 23 years at the time of accident.
Unfortunately, at such young age he has suffered whole body disability to the extent of 18%, with which he has to lead his entire life.

Therefore, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.60,000/-
under this head.
23. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
During the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that the plants have removed.

Further the Ex.P.19-Discharge summary, it is clearly mentioned the petitioner was admitted on 20.07.2023 and discharged on 24.07.2023 and on 21.07.2023 he was underwent surgery wherein implant removed.
Hence no amount is granted under the head of future medical expenses.

24. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up period : 7,100-00 3 Pain & sufferings :
60,000-00 4 Attendant charges, extra nutritious : 15,000-00 food & conveyance charges 5
Medical expenses : 42,000-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 60,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 1,84,100-00 25.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
26. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-40-N-1854 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Hence this issue Suhas.R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39698896/
6 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,84,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
